title: TOC entries show stray text when a heading contains an HTML tag whose attribute value includes ">"
spec: This is the Python-Markdown library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 run_tests.py`. With the `toc` extension, a heading containing inline HTML whose quoted attribute value has a `>` gets a garbled TOC name, label and id. Example 1: ```python md = markdown.Markdown(extensions=['toc']) md.convert('# Python support') print(md.toc); print(md.toc_tokens[0]['name'], md.toc_tokens[0]['id']) ``` EXPECTED: link `Python support`, name `Python support`, id `python-support`. ACTUAL: name is `3">Python support`, id is `3python-support`, link text is `3">Python support`. Example 2 (custom label via attr_list): ```python md = markdown.Markdown(extensions=['toc', 'attr_list']) md.convert('''# Python support {data-toc-label='Python & support'}''') print(md.toc_tokens[0]['name']) ``` EXPECTED: `Python & support` (TOC link text `Python & support`). ACTUAL: `3">Python & support`. Rule: when TOC names are derived from heading text or `data-toc-label`, HTML tags must be removed as whole tags, so a `>` inside a single- or double-quoted attribute value does not end the tag. The `html` field in `toc_tokens` and the rendered heading are unchanged.
acceptance: A heading with `<abbr title="Python > 3">Python</abbr> support` (double or single quotes) yields TOC name `Python support` and id `python-support`.
A `data-toc-label` containing a tag with `>` in a quoted attribute gives a clean TOC name, e.g. `Python & support`.
Existing TOC tests still pass (`python3 run_tests.py`).
